t.1.69.1: Then at daybreak Janaka, skilled in speech, having performed his rites together with the great sages, spoke these words to Śatānanda, his family priest.
t.1.69.2: My younger brother, exceedingly righteous and of great splendor, renowned as Kuśadhvaja, dwelt in a beautiful city.
t.1.69.4: I wish to see him; he is regarded by me as the protector of the sacrifice. Let that one of great splendour also enjoy this delight together with me.
t.1.69.3: Drinking the waters of the river Ikṣumatī, whose waters reach up to the palisades, he dwells in holy Sāṃkāśyā, a city resplendent with merit, like the aerial chariot Puṣpaka.
t.1.69.5: At the command of the lord of men, they set out with swift horses to bring back that tiger among men, just as others once went at Indra's order to fetch Viṣṇu.
t.1.69.6: At the command of the lord of men, Kuśadhvaja came.
t.1.69.7: He saw the great-souled Janaka, devoted to dharma; and having saluted Śatānanda and also the righteous king, he
t.1.69.9: The two heroes dispatched Sudāmana, the foremost of ministers, saying: "Go quickly, O lord of ministers, and bring here the Aikṣvāka of boundless splendour, the invincible one, together with his sons and with his ministers."
t.1.69.8: He ascended the supreme, divine seat worthy of a king, and both those brothers of immeasurable might were seated.
t.1.69.10: Having gone to the royal lodging, he saw the one who increased the line of the Raghus, and bowing to him with his head, he spoke these words.
t.1.69.12: Having heard the words of the best of ministers, the king, together with the hosts of sages and with his kinsmen, then went to the place where Janaka was.
t.1.69.11: O hero, lord of Ayodhyā, the Vaideha, lord of Mithilā, has resolved to see you together with your preceptors and family priests.
t.1.69.13: That king, foremost among those skilled in speech, accompanied by his ministers, together with his preceptors and his kinsmen, spoke these words to the king of Videha.
t.1.69.14: As you know, great king, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha, the family deity of the Ikṣvākus, is our spokesman in all matters.
t.1.69.16: When Daśaratha had fallen silent, the blessed seer Vasiṣṭha, skilled in speech, addressed these words to the king of Videha and his family priest.
t.1.69.15: With the permission of Viśvāmitra, and together with all the great sages, this righteous-souled Vasiṣṭha will relate my lineage in due order.
t.1.69.18: From Kaśyapa was born Vivasvān, and Manu is known as Vaivasvata, the son of Vivasvān. Manu was formerly a Prajāpati, and Ikṣvāku was the son of Manu.
t.1.69.17: Brahmā, whose source is the Unmanifest, is everlasting and imperishable, O constant one. From him Marīci was born, and from Marīci came his son Kaśyapa.
t.1.69.19: Know that Ikṣvāku to have been the first king in Ayodhyā. To Ikṣvāku was born a glorious son, Vikukṣi.
t.1.69.20: From Vikukṣi was born a son, the greatly radiant and mighty Bāṇa; and of Bāṇa the son was the greatly radiant and mighty Anaraṇya.
t.1.69.21: From Anaraṇya was born Pṛthu, and Triśaṅku was the son of Pṛthu. To Triśaṅku was born a son, the greatly renowned Dhundhumāra.
t.1.69.22: From Dhundhumāra was born the greatly radiant Yuvanāśva, a mighty chariot-warrior; the son of Yuvanāśva was the glorious Māndhātā, lord of the earth.
t.1.69.23: To Māndhātṛ was born a glorious son, Susaṃdhi. Susaṃdhi in turn had two sons, Dhruvasaṃdhi and Prasenajit.
t.1.69.24: From Dhruvasaṃdhi was born the illustrious one named Bharata by name; and from Bharata was born the greatly radiant one named Asita.
t.1.69.25: Because he was born together with that very poison, he became Sagara. To Sagara was born Asamañja, and from Asamañja came Aṃśumān.
t.1.69.26: Dilīpa was the son of Aṃśumant, and Dilīpa's son was Bhagīratha. From Bhagīratha came Kakutstha, and likewise Kakutstha's son was Raghu.
t.1.69.27: The son of Raghu was the radiant Kalmāṣapāda, who grew mighty and became a man-eater; from him was born Śaṅkhaṇa.
t.1.69.28: Sudarśana was the son of Śaṅkhaṇa, and Agnivarṇa was born of Sudarśana; Śīghraga was the son of Agnivarṇa, and Maru was the son of Śīghraga.
t.1.69.29: From Maru came Praśuśruka, and from Praśuśruka came Ambarīṣa. The son of Ambarīṣa was Nahuṣa, lord of the earth.
t.1.69.30: Of Nahuṣa was born Yayāti, and Nābhāga was the son of Yayāti. Of Nābhāga was born Aja, and from Aja came Daśaratha. From that Daśaratha were born the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.1.69.31: Of the kings born in the family of Ikṣvāku, pure in their lineage from its very beginning, supremely righteous, heroic, and speakers of truth.
t.1.69.32: O king, I ask for your daughters on behalf of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; O best of men, you should give these worthy maidens to the two who are worthy of them.
